# protocol/

Language-neutral protocol files shared by every Syncky component: the relay, the phone app, the agents and the servers. When a vector and prose disagree on byte-level behavior, the vector wins.

**Do not edit generated files by hand.** `types.json`, `units.json`, `messages.json` and every vector file except the RFC 9180 one are generated by the Syncky core and checked against it there; the schemas and the RFC file are hand-written. Table generation derives message types, marker mappings and size limits from protocol definitions and checks canonical field order and both AAD uses against existing vectors.

## Relay queue capacity

`GET /v1/messages` (E11) may include an optional outer `queue` object alongside `messages`, `next_after`, `has_more`, `undelivered` and activity metadata. Updated relays emit it on every successful agent or device page, including empty and paginated pages:

```json
{
  "queue": {
    "hub_bytes": 12000000,
    "sender_rows": 206,
    "max_hub_bytes": 67108864,
    "max_sender_rows": 10000,
    "as_of": "2026-10-30T09:00:00Z"
  }
}
```

| Field | Units and scope |
| --- | --- |
| `hub_bytes` | UTF-8 bytes of general-lane stored bodies across every sender, including unmarked data/control and ordinary system rows; excludes marked traffic, its derived expiry events, delivery-row overhead and the delivered `seq` field |
| `sender_rows` | General-lane stored rows sent by the authenticated caller, counted once regardless of recipient count; excludes marked traffic and its derived expiry events; an agent never sees a phone's row count |
| `max_hub_bytes` | Configured hub byte cap; default 67108864 bytes (64 MiB) |
| `max_sender_rows` | Configured per-sender row cap; default 10000 rows |
| `as_of` | Relay UTC observation timestamp, sampled in the same transaction as the page and usage |

Usage values are nonnegative safe integers; caps are positive safe integers. Stored bodies include expired unswept rows and held rows until deletion. Fetching alone frees no capacity. A transport acknowledgement or committed successful webhook delivery frees a body only when its final delivery is removed; maintenance, purge and revocation can also remove bodies. `undelivered` remains a per-recipient display aggregate and activity's live waiting count excludes expired rows; neither substitutes for capacity accounting. A snapshot describes observed storage, reserves no space and can change before the next upload.

`POST /v1/messages` (E10) adds `details.reason: "queue_full"` only when the caller's stored-row cap or the hub's byte cap refuses a new envelope. Both refusals retain HTTP 429, `Retry-After: 300` and this body:

```json
{"error":"rate_limited","message":"Too many requests","details":{"retry_after_s":300,"reason":"queue_full"}}
```

An identical accepted-body retry still returns `200` with `duplicate: true` before capacity enforcement. Unmarked data/control and ordinary system rows share the general caps. Marked traffic and its unmarked derived expiry events use separate diagnostics accounting; E11 adds no diagnostics queue snapshot. Diagnostics quota/cap refusals use the distinct reasons documented below. Other rate limits retain their existing details without this reason; a 300-second delay alone does not identify a full queue. Fetches and transport acknowledgements remain available subject to their ordinary limits.

Both additions are optional for compatibility: old clients ignore unknown outer fields/details, and new clients accept pages and errors without them. An absent snapshot means unknown usage, not zero; an absent reason retains ordinary rate-limit handling. These fields do not alter envelopes, encrypted inner messages or control reasons. There is no existing outer MessagePage or generic HTTP-error JSON schema/vector to update; `envelope-shape.json` covers submitted envelopes. The minimal server handles direct webhook delivery and has no relay page/error mirror. The generated-file rules and vector precedence above remain unchanged.

## Relay change hints

The optional E21 connection tells a connected member its relay queue changed so it can fetch sooner. It carries no envelopes, ciphertext, sequence numbers or acknowledgments. Fetch with `GET /v1/messages` (E11) and acknowledge with `POST /v1/acks` (E12).

To check for a command acknowledgment, send `command_ack=1` on E11 with the acknowledged cursor or omit `after`. For 15 minutes after the caller's last committed data send to a phone, Relay allows an early fetch if the previous fetch preceded that send or at least 25 seconds have passed since the previous fetch. Request limits and Retry-After still apply.

A refusal based on the E11 poll interval returns `429 rate_limited` with `details.reason: "agent_poll_floor"`. A client may recheck with `command_ack=1` after a command is sent successfully following that refused request. Continue to honor Retry-After from other rate limits, including refusals without a reason.

Connect to the relay origin with `wss://` (`ws://` only for an HTTP relay) and path `/v1/socket`, with the member bearer in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` request header; there is no query credential or subprotocol. Before the upgrade the relay answers with ordinary JSON errors: `426 upgrade_required` with `Upgrade: websocket` when the `Upgrade` header is missing, `400 invalid_request` for another `Upgrade` value or a request body, `401 invalid_token` for an unknown or inactive bearer, and `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After` when the per-token request limit is reached. The app-version check applies as on every other route. Every upgrade attempt with an active bearer counts toward the same per-token request limit as other calls, including one refused with 429 or closed with 4403. The route ignores App Attest assertions and has no CORS support.

| Direction | Text frame | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| relay → client | `changed` | The relay committed a change that gave this member a new delivery (a new envelope or system event, or a delivery released again after a hold), or a phone completed a pairing this agent created. At most one per member per relay transaction. Hints carry no data and may be coalesced, repeated or lost; a hint means "fetch now", never what to fetch. |
| relay → phone | `first_sync_ready` | Sent once after admission: this relay accepts the phone's first-sync frames. |
| relay → agent | `first_sync` | The relay is holding this agent's connection open while a newly joined phone finishes its first sync. |
| client → relay | `ping` | The relay answers `pong`. The Syncky agent sends `ping` every 30 seconds and treats two missed `pong`s as a lost connection. |
| phone → relay | `first_sync`, `first_sync_done` | The phone's first sync after joining has started or finished. Any other client frame closes the connection with 1008. |

| Close code | Meaning | Client action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4401 | The member is no longer active, or the hub is being deleted. | Stop using the connection. An ordinary HTTP call reports the actual state (`invalid_token`, hub events); the close itself is not proof of revocation. |
| 4403 | The relay accepted the handshake but grants no lease to this member now, or ended a first-sync hold (close reason `first_sync_done` when the phone finishes; no close reason when the phone's connection ends). | Keep polling. Do not reconnect until a new reason for a lease applies. |
| 4408 | The lease ended. | Reconnect only if a reason for a lease still applies. |
| 4409 | A newer connection for the same member replaced this one. | Leave the newer connection in place. |
| 1008 | The client sent a frame the relay does not accept from it. | Fix the client. |
| 1011 | The relay could not keep the connection. | Treat it as a lost connection. |

A failed handshake or a lost connection means "keep polling". It never means revocation: a client usually cannot see the HTTP status of a refused upgrade, so only an ordinary HTTP response decides `invalid_token` or hub revocation. Reconnect with jittered exponential backoff and a small bounded number of attempts, and honor every `Retry-After` from HTTP calls.

The relay keeps at most one connection per member; a successful admission replaces the previous connection with 4409. A phone receives a 30-minute lease. An agent receives a lease only while it has a reason: a pending pairing it created (until that link expires), the 15 minutes after a phone joins the hub, or the 15 minutes after its own last accepted data envelope addressed to at least one phone. Control envelopes and sends addressed only to other agents do not count. The lease ends at the latest of these deadlines, at most 15 minutes after admission. While a phone that joined the hub in the last 24 hours holds a connection and has sent `first_sync` without `first_sync_done`, the relay sends each agent `first_sync` and extends its lease in 15-minute steps; it closes the agent with 4403 as soon as that phone finishes, or when its connection ends unless the agent's own lease still runs. An agent receives at most 32 leases per UTC day. Outside these rules the upgrade completes and the relay closes at once with 4403. A lease is not a poll: E11 remains the activity heartbeat, so keep polling at the configured cadence.

Subscribe first, then catch up with one E11 fetch, because a change committed before the connection opened sends no hint. With the relay's agent poll floor enabled, an admitted agent connection may take one opening page through the floor: the request must start at the agent's acknowledged cursor (omit `after` or pass that cursor), and the agent must not have used such an opening bypass within the preceding floor interval, so reconnecting does not grant another. Each hint sent to the agent grants one more opening page, except a hint caused by the agent's own E10. Further pages follow ordinary `has_more` pagination. Token RPM and `Retry-After` still apply, and a page the floor already allows keeps its ordinary handling. Phone fetches have no agent poll floor. The Syncky agent connects only during bounded windows and has a local `fast_path` setting to turn the connection off; see [transport limits](../agent/docs/REFERENCE.md#limits-and-transport).

## How the agent reads these files

The thin agent loads its bundled or signature-verified message table and inner schemas together with the skill. From this release onward, `send --validate` and MCP `syncky_send` with `validate: true` check available local schemas with bundled Ajv 2020 and send nothing. For a local check, first confirm that the installed `help send` output or MCP tool description says validation sends nothing. Both the CLI and MCP validate scope releases and access requests before sending. Receiving validates transport/authentication and a JSON object with a string `type`, preserving unknown fields without feature-schema parsing. It performs no unit conversion, Health policy checks, series reassembly or summaries. [`agent/src/protocol-files.js`](../agent/src/protocol-files.js) resolves standalone vector files relative to the package; `SYNCKY_PROTOCOL_DIR` selects another copy for selftest.

`syncky-agent selftest` checks crypto, keys, envelope shape/AAD/markers, pairing, App Attest clientData and webhook signatures (exit 4 on failure). Feature normalization, command policy and reassembly belong to phone/schema conformance tests; agent vector tests prove raw preservation. [`agent/AGENTS.md`](../agent/AGENTS.md) describes the transport boundary and [`agent/docs/REFERENCE.md`](../agent/docs/REFERENCE.md) lists limits and errors.

## Vector files and case naming

Pair links use `https://syncky.app/pair` with path exactly `/pair`, no query and parameters only in the fragment, or, for parsing only, the case-sensitive legacy scheme `syncky`. Pair builders always emit HTTPS; an explicit scheme selects only the site. Webhook builders use `https://syncky.app/connect#…` by default. Put all setup parameters in the fragment and omit the outer query, including a bare `?`. The app requires review and explicit confirmation before adding a server. Custom-scheme pair links require an explicit scan inside Syncky or paste with preview and consent. They cannot start pairing by tapping or through the system Camera. The link form does not change relay trust policy.

- Generated vector files are `{"format":1,"generated_by":"syncky-core GenerateProtocolArtifacts","cases":[…]}`. `keys.json` is a map `agent`/`dev1`/`dev2`/`mallory` → `{ikm, sk, pk, member_id}`; the RFC file keeps the upstream hex layout.
- Binary values are unpadded base64url; RFC data stays hex. In `app-attest-client-data.json`, `body` encodes the exact request bytes (empty is `""`) and `client_data_sha256` encodes the 32 digest bytes; hashes embedded in `client_data` are lowercase hexadecimal text. On the App Attest wire, Apple's `key_id`, `attestation` and assertion object use standard base64 with padding, while `challenge` and the pairing `public_key` use base64url. This file contains no Apple objects. Compare private keys across libraries through the derived public key: `sk` and `sk_e` are the raw, unclamped RFC 9180 `DeriveKeyPair` output.
- Case `name`s are lowercase snake_case (`^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.-]{0,127}$`), unique within a file, and describe the input. Report failures by case name, not by index; regeneration may insert cases.
- `app-attest-client-data.json` uses `attestation_*` and `assertion_*` names with lowercase letters, digits and underscores only. Dispatch by `kind` (`attestation` or `assertion`); every case expects the exact UTF-8 `client_data` bytes and their `client_data_sha256`, without JSON parsing or reserialization of the decoded `body`. All fixtures are public and synthetic; replay checks canonicalization only and adds no agent attestation support.
- Classify cases by their expectation field, never by name. `valid_*` / `valid*` prefixes mark most accepting cases in `envelope-shape.json`, `pair-uris.json` and `webhook-signatures.json`, but some accepting cases are named after the rule they exercise (`created_at_lowercase_t`, `duplicate_key_last_value_wins`, `unicode_body`, `empty_body`). In `pair-uris.json`, `build_*` cases carry `input` and the canonical `uri` instead of `expect`. `series-parts.json` names the kind and the situation (`route_missing_a_part`, `heartbeat_series_in_reverse_order`). `inner-messages.json` uses `sync_*` / `commands_*` for parseable messages (`sync_drop_*` and `commands_drop_rules` exercise element drops), `invalid_*` / `unsupported_*` for message-level failures and `system_*` for system messages; the `system_*` and `diagnostics_*` cases carry `kind` (`data` or `control`, the envelope kind the parser is told; absent means `data`). `fingerprints.json` has the three key-pair cases plus `extra_*` edge cases; `pair-codes.json` has one secret with the three device keys (same code, three proofs) plus `extra_*` cases for a zero-padded group, both orders of the decoy offsets and a decoy that wraps past 999. `envelopes-negative.json` names the mutation (`tag_byte_flipped`, `hub_changed`, `kind_data_relabelled_as_control`, …) and carries a prose `mutation` field. `bridge-json.json` groups cases by `kind`, including marked-link parse output and `pairing_prepare_error` snapshots of the core exception code and message. `command-policy.json` names the type and the rule (`water_millilitres`, `cholesterol_milligrams`, `conversion_overflows_to_infinity`). `webhook-requests.json` names the format first (`native_*`, `hae_*`, `csv_*`, `influx_*`).
- Expectation fields: `envelopes-negative.json` `expect` is the open error code (`aead_failed`, `hpke_open_failed`, `malformed`, `not_a_recipient`, `unknown_sender`); `envelope-shape.json` `expect` is the relay response (`status`, plus `error`/`field` for 400 or `member_ids` for 404); `inner-messages.json` `expect` is `ok`, `invalid` or `unsupported_version`; `series-parts.json` `expect` is `ok`, `incomplete` or `inconsistent`: `series` is the whole boundary sample (no `part`/`parts`), `parts` the wire parts cut at `max_part_bytes`, `reassembled` the whole sample they give back, `conflicts` extra wire parts that differ from a committed one, and `arrival` the order in which `{"part": i}` and `{"conflict": i}` reach one device's reassembler; `webhook-signatures.json` `expect` is `valid`, `bad_signature` or `stale`; `command-policy.json` `expect` is `allow` or `reject` (with `reason` and optional `detail`), and an allowed quantity write carries the converted `value` and the catalog `unit`. `webhook-requests.json` has no `expect`: each case carries the destination, its `secrets`, the `collected` changes and `max_request_bytes` in, and the `requests` (with their anchor `groups`) and the `report` counts out; a native body is the canonical sync message of the install `device` plus a `delivery` object; an `hae` case adds the delivery's `session_id` (the `session-id` header of every request) and its bodies are Health Auto Export `{"data":{"metrics":[…],"workouts":[…]}}` with deletions and unmapped types counted in `dropped`; a `csv` body is RFC 4180 rows under the fixed header and an `influx` body is line protocol, both without a `delivery` object, with the object kinds counted in `report.skipped_kinds` (0 for native and HAE). Every `destination` carries `send_deletions`; `accept_writes` and `write_types` are left out because they do not change a request. Every case also carries `link`, the webhook configuration link of its destination and secrets, with the selected site (default `https://syncky.app/connect#…`).
- Optional case-level `resend` in `webhook-requests.json` is a Boolean delivery input, default `false`. When true, every native request adds `delivery.resend: true` before size fitting and signing; false omits the field. HAE, CSV and Influx keep their bodies and headers, Check connection never adds the marker, and export files have no `delivery` block. Delivery indices/counts and `more` cover one delivery call even when a chosen-period operation uses several calls. Resend cases include signed split native requests and unchanged non-native bodies.
- Optional native-only `summaries` in `webhook-requests.json` is a separate direct-history input, alongside unchanged `collected`. Request/report `summaries` counts are independent of raw `samples` and default to zero when absent; summary-only requests may have empty `groups`. The signed summary-only, mixed and split cases retain per-call `more`, index and count semantics. Supporting receivers replace by `(device, type, unit, start, end, stat)`; legacy inner parsers ignore the array. A relay sync message uses the same array for interval sums (see the rules below). See [server.md](server.md#daily-quantity-summaries-in-native-history) for compatibility.
- `bridge-json.json` adds `core_tools_export_fragment` for encoded native/HAE/CSV streams and recursive envelope descriptors, and `webhook_delivery_report` for the direct-history result. Fragment streams contain already encoded elements/CSV rows. Envelopes provide prefix, suffix, separator, optional stream id, children and whether an empty container is required, so file writers can spool streams and assemble a single document with bounded copy buffers. Native omits an empty summary array; CSV emits one header and escaped/formula-protected CRLF rows in day-stream order. Native/HAE fragments preserve document semantics; CSV preserves parsed row multisets rather than global type order. Raw-object, daily-summary and expected-format-omission counts are separate. Streamed local files publish only when finished and retry the entire original period after error/cancellation; direct-server restart uses the last complete day after cool-down. See [full-depth periods and local files](server.md#full-depth-periods-and-local-files) for foreground and byte/count semantics.
- Optional `url_scheme` is a builder argument. In `pair-uris.json` it belongs only to build `input`: Absence infers the HTTPS pairing site from the relay; explicit `syncky` selects `https://syncky.app/pair#<payload>`. Builders never emit the legacy `syncky://pair?<payload>` form; it stays parse-only. Both versions have parse cases for HTTPS and the legacy scheme, and build cases for HTTPS. Pair parse output never includes the builder argument or envelope identity, so exclude `url_scheme` when comparing build input to parsed fields. In `webhook-requests.json` the argument remains case-level, absence selects `syncky.app`, and selection changes only the authority of the HTTPS `link`, leaving request bodies and headers unchanged.
- Compare JSON results structurally (key order free, numbers by value; `command-policy.json` values are doubles that the JVM and JS spell differently), except where a case says byte-exact: pair-URI `build_*` `uri`, the positive envelopes' `enc`/`wrapped_key`/`ciphertext` on re-seal, `webhook-signatures.json` `signature`, and `webhook-requests.json` request `body`, `headers` and `link` (the signature covers the exact body bytes; header order is the order the core sends).

## Pairing access outcomes and compatibility

New v2 links carry `v,r,h,t,k,n,c`, optional `a=1` when the requested scope is on the relay, and optional `s=http` in the existing HTTPS fragment or explicit in-app scheme format. Each new pairing uses a fresh 16-byte secret `c`, including bare v2 links. The agent encrypts the request with a key derived from the link secret and sends the ciphertext to the relay in E2 as `pairing_scope_blob` and requires `pairing_scope_stored: true` before giving the owner the link. E2 retries reuse the serialized body. E2 and E4 have a hosted body cap of 16384 UTF-8 bytes. The encrypted scope is at most 12000 decoded bytes or 16000 base64url characters. Bare pairings and new v1 pairings omit the blob.

The phone opts in via `include_pairing_scope: true` on E4 only for `a=1` links. A current parser treats `a` as a known key with no duplicates and accepts only `a=1` on v2 without legacy inline scope. The builder places it after `c` and before `s`. Bare links use legacy E4. An upgraded relay returns `pairing_scope_blob` as a string or JSON null. Omitting the option or setting it false keeps the legacy response, and E3 never includes the blob. The relay clears the blob on every successful join, including a legacy join, or on expiry cleanup. At defaults a pending row lives 600 seconds, with a maximum of five open rows and 80000 encoded ciphertext characters per hub. Completion metadata retains its separate lifetime. Only the ciphertext is stored on the relay, alongside ordinary pairing metadata. The relay can block the join or withhold the request, but `a=1` makes the request mandatory for the phone and prevents silent fallback to bare pairing. A null blob gives `pairing_scope_missing`. An absent field gives `pairing_scope_relay_unsupported`. Both revoke the consumed join, as do invalid bytes or failed authentication. The link and QR still carry pairing credentials and the decryption secret.

The phone authenticates the joined agent against the link and verifies the scope before review. The joined draft has a 15-minute review window and resumes locally. The owner sees the exact Read/Write types before device proof, Health authorization or any access grant. Choices apply only to the requesting agent. An interrupted Health sheet keeps the review and choices so the owner can tap Allow again. Pairing choices have no quota and a type declined at pairing starts the same seven-day wait. The phone commits the decision before the code/proof flow and sends a standard `access_reply` with per-item `allowed`, `declined` or `needs_health_settings` for the pairing reference. Strict `pair_proof` and `confirmed` messages retain their existing shapes. Only authenticated `sync.scope` establishes effective scope, including empty grants. The phone can send it promptly without collecting samples or a manual initial Sync. Health read authorization remains unobservable.

| Compatibility path | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Syncky 0.1.5, new scoped v2 link, upgraded relay | The old parser ignores `a=1`. Legacy E4 completes without delivering scope. Confirm the pairing, then choose Health data on the phone or update Syncky and ask the agent for an ordinary access request. |
| New phone, valid old inline v1/v2 link | Review still precedes legacy E4 during the transition. The phone retains the original confirmation and pairing reply behavior. |
| Old agent and phone, upgraded relay | E2/E3/E4 retain the old shapes when scope is omitted and the phone does not opt in. |
| Syncky 0.1.5, ordinary access request above 4096 bytes | Relay acceptance or transport ACK can succeed while the phone drops the request. Update the phone, choose Health data on it, or use a request that fits 4096 bytes. |
| Upgraded relay withholds the blob | A phone opening an `a=1` link revokes the join on a null response. Ask your agent for a new pairing link. |
| Old relay | The new scoped agent withholds the link without the E2 receipt. The new staged-v2 phone detects a missing E4 field and cleans up the join. Try again later or contact Syncky support. An old relay can also refuse an access envelope above 4096 bytes with HTTP 413. |
| New `pair --v1` with scope flags | The link omits scope. Once the owner verifies the phone fingerprint and the relay accepts `confirmed`, the agent sends one ordinary `access_request` with a fresh ref and a 24-hour TTL. Retries reuse its reference, message id and sealed body. |

A confirmed v2 pairing without a reply stays confirmed. The thin agent retains the ref and reports `awaiting`, then `no_reply` at its 15-minute post-confirmation deadline. A late matching reply remains usable. A follow-up uses a fresh ref and a finite positive TTL up to 24 hours (`0 < expires_at - created_at <= 24h`) with renewed explicit owner approval and phone availability. Missing replies alone convey neither decline nor phone version. See the [agent setup guide](../agent/SETUP.md#5-pair-the-owners-iphone).

The thin agent uses bounded 300-second response polling for scoped v2 pairing and sent access/diagnostics requests, separate from the 25-second first-sync join window and configured cadence. With a relay that supports early checks, the agent can check for a command acknowledgment immediately after sending and then every 25 seconds until the acknowledgment arrives or the 15-minute wait expires. `receive --once` bypasses configured cadence while preserving the floor, Retry-After and existing exceptions. Deferral exposes `reason` (`poll_floor` or `retry_after`) and `next_poll_at`. Matching responses or expiry finish only their own waits. See [transport limits](../agent/docs/REFERENCE.md#limits-and-transport).

The [minimal agent](../examples/minimal-agent/README.md) and [browser demo](../examples/browser-demo/README.md) create bare links. Their low-level URI fixtures cover legacy inline compatibility. Reopen the HTTPS link, copy it and paste it in Syncky, or scan the agent’s QR code inside Syncky. The HTTPS fragment stays out of the browser's request to the pairing page.

### Encrypted pairing scope v1

- The plaintext is compact UTF-8 JSON with exactly `{"request_ref":"<32 lowercase hex>","read":[…],"write":[…]}` in that field order, without a BOM or trailing newline. Sort each side in ASCII order and deduplicate before encoding. Either side can be empty and at least one item is required. The same name can occur on both sides if writable. Read accepts known catalog scope names, including `workout` and characteristics. Write accepts only writable names. Receivers require strict UTF-8, the exact shape and byte-for-byte canonical reserialization.
- Derive a 32-byte key with HKDF-SHA256 from the 16 decoded bytes of `c`, ASCII salt `syncky-pairing-scope-v1` and ASCII info `syncky-pairing-scope-v1/key`. Use ChaCha20-Poly1305 with a fresh independent 12-byte nonce and a 16-byte tag. The exact ASCII AAD is `syncky-pairing-scope-v1|<hub_id>|<agent_public_key>`, using the canonical hub id and unpadded base64url of the 32-byte X25519 public key. Salt, info and AAD have no terminators.
- The blob is canonical unpadded base64url of `nonce[12] || ciphertext || tag[16]`. Its structural range is 29–12000 decoded bytes, leaving at most 11972 plaintext bytes. The [blob vectors](test-vectors/pairing-scope.json) pin canonical and whole-catalog bytes, wrong secret/hub/key/version, nonce/ciphertext/tag tampering, encoding and size limits, and authenticated invalid plaintext.
- The pairing fit check budgets the synthetic no-reason request and largest pairing reply against the 131072-byte access cap. Pairing decisions have no amendment or alias and the synthetic request stays off the wire. The complete current catalog fits in one encrypted pairing or one ordinary request. The [transport table guide](messages.md#format) defines the access override and the ordinary 4096-byte control cap.

## [KMP-defined] rules other implementations must mirror

The Syncky core defined these details where the wire spec left them open; the vectors pin each relevant implementation's behavior. Transport implementations mirror envelope, authentication and pairing rules. Phone parsers and consumers that normalize Health data or reassemble parts mirror the corresponding feature rules. The thin agent retains raw incoming JSON without applying that normalization, policy or reassembly.

- **App Attest clientData** (`app-attest-client-data.json`): join UTF-8 fields with one LF and no trailing LF. Attestation fields are `syncky-attest-v1`, the unchanged `challenge`, `hub_id`, unchanged `public_key`, and lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 `pairing_token`. Assertion fields are `syncky-assert-v1`, uppercase `method`, the actual URL pathname (including any base prefix, excluding query), lowercase hex SHA-256 of the decoded `body`, lowercase hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bearer `token`, and canonical nonnegative decimal `timestamp_ms` (no sign, leading zeros or exponent). Hash those exact clientData bytes with SHA-256 for Apple. Request-body whitespace and Unicode bytes remain significant; the empty DELETE body hashes zero bytes. The timestamp is part of the hashed input, so changing it changes the digest. The assertion header is `<timestamp_ms>.<standard-base64 assertion object>`; the vector's digest encoding does not change that wire encoding.
- **Envelope shape pointers** (`envelope-shape.json`): the first failure wins, in this order: unparsable or non-object → `field: ""`; first unknown top-level key in document order, then first missing key in the order `v, msg_id, kind, from, created_at, recipients, nonce, ciphertext` → `/<key>`; then `v` (value-based integer 1, so `1.0` and `1e0` pass), `msg_id` (UUIDv7), `kind` (`data` or `control`, case-sensitive), `from` (= caller), `created_at` (RFC 3339 accept form); `recipients` (array of 1..7) and then per index `/recipients/<i>` (not an object), `/recipients/<i>/<key>` (unknown, then missing in the order `member_id, enc, wrapped_key`; bad, duplicate or equal to `from`; `enc` 32 bytes; `wrapped_key` 48 bytes); `/nonce` (12 bytes), `/ciphertext` (≥ 16 bytes). Recipients not in the active member set → `404 unknown_recipient` with all of them in `member_ids`, in recipient order, matched by string only. 413 (including the 4096-byte ordinary control cap and 131072-byte access control cap, checked after every 400 rule and before 404) and idempotency are relay-only and not in the vectors. A case carries either `envelope` (send its compact serialization) or `raw` (send the exact text).
- **Strict JSON** (`envelope-shape.json` `raw_*` cases): a body outside RFC 8259 is unparseable (`field: ""`), including a leading BOM (Fetch `text()`/`json()` strip it silently, so the relay must check the first bytes itself) and nesting deeper than 128 containers. Duplicate keys keep the last value, as `JSON.parse` does. Unknown-key pointers use RFC 6901 escaping (`a/b` → `/a~1b`, `m~x` → `/m~0x`, the empty key → `/`).
- **Inner parsing, `normalized` and `dropped`** (`inner-messages.json`): message-level `invalid` vs `unsupported_version` (`v` checked before `type`); invalid elements are dropped and listed as JSON pointers (`/samples/3`, `/deleted/0`, `/acks/1`, `/commands/2`) while the message stays `ok`. `normalized` is the canonical re-emission: all four sync arrays and `more` present (`summaries` only when it has elements), unknown fields removed, timestamps in the emit form, integral numbers as integers, ack `version` omitted when absent, command fields kept raw (unknown keys after the known ones) except known-field timestamp normalization and a non-finite number becoming `null`. "Present" means the key exists, so `samples: null` or `more: null` is `invalid`. A `normalized` value parses back to itself (an unknown system type drops `/type` again on re-parse).
- **System messages** (`inner-messages.json` `system_*`): parsed with the envelope kind. In a `control` envelope the nine named types are strict (exact key set, closed `reason` enums, `resync_request.from` emitted in the canonical UTC form, `agent_info.version` matching `^[0-9A-Za-z.+_-]{1,64}$`, `pair_proof.proof` canonical base64url of exactly 32 bytes, `scope_release.read`/`write` as described under Scope release); any other type matching `^[a-z_]{1,32}$` is `ok`, normalized to `{"v":1,"type":…}` with `/type` in `dropped`; `sync`/`commands` and anything else are `invalid` at `/type`. In a `data` envelope a system type is `invalid`.

Phone command parsing allows at most 32 nested object/array containers, including the command object, before normalization or retention of unknown fields. A deeper command is dropped as an invalid field; ordinary siblings remain usable. Shallow unknown fields remain preserved. This applies to agent commands, direct-server replies and single-command evaluation; the complete JSON document limit remains 128 containers.

Before replacing phone or direct-server durable state, the receiver validates the complete serialized candidate with its corresponding loader. An invalid candidate fails with `storage` and the fixed reason `state_candidate_invalid`, preserving last-good durable bytes. The run's cursor is not committed; the same envelope can be fetched again on a later run. This guard prevents corrupt replacement and does not automatically repair old corrupt state or discard an otherwise unhandled poison item.

- **Control envelope AAD** (`envelopes.json` `control_*`, `envelopes-negative.json` `kind_*_relabelled_as_*`): `syncky-v1|<hub>|<msg_id>|<from>|control`; unmarked data AAD has no suffix, so changing `kind` either way fails with `hpke_open_failed`.
- **Open errors** (`envelopes-negative.json`): checked in the order `not_a_recipient` → `unknown_sender` → `malformed` (only the receiver's own `enc`/`wrapped_key`, then `nonce`, then `ciphertext`) → `hpke_open_failed` → `aead_failed`; a successful open whose plaintext fails the inner parser yields `inner_invalid` or `unsupported_version`.
- **Pair-URI envelopes and errors** (`pair-uris.json`): legacy links check scheme → host exactly `pair` → fragment refusal. Links use `https://syncky.app/pair`. A parser may also accept `<label>.syncky.app` only when bound to relay `relay-<label>.syncky.app`. The agent accepts legacy `syncky-<label>` with that matching relay or any valid relay outside `syncky.app`; other relays within `syncky.app` are refused for that labelled scheme. A builder given `syncky-<label>` follows the same relay rule and emits `<label>.syncky.app`; beside a relay outside `syncky.app` the scheme alone chooses that site, which this relay-bound parser rule does not accept. `syncky://` accepts any valid relay. HTTPS checks scheme exactly `https` → raw authority `syncky.app` or the relay-bound site → raw path exactly `/pair` → no outer query, including a bare `?`. Userinfo, explicit ports, host case changes, trailing dots, lookalikes, escaped paths, dot segments and backslashes are rejected without normalization. HTTPS parameters come only from the fragment; a missing or empty fragment reaches missing `v`. The site identity never grants relay trust.
  Both link formats then share the same checks: traverse payload segments in order, rejecting a duplicate known key before decoding its repeated value and rejecting malformed encoding as encountered; then `v`, `unsupported_version`, missing `r h t k n`, missing `c` (v2), value checks `r h t k n`, `c` (v2), `s`, `insecure_relay`. Errors are `{"ok":false,"error":"invalid_uri","param":<p>}`, where `param` is the offending payload parameter (`v`, `r`, `h`, `t`, `k`, `n`, `c`, `s`, `request_ref`, `read`, `write`, `scope`) or `scheme`, `host`, `path`, `query`, `fragment`, `encoding`; `unsupported_version` applies to `v` other than `1` and `2`. `c` is known in both versions, so a duplicate or badly encoded `c` always fails; its value is checked (canonical base64url of exactly 16 bytes) and returned as `pair_secret` only for `v=2`. `s=http` describes the relay transport while the outer HTTPS link stays HTTPS; it gives `insecure_relay` when `allow_insecure` is false. Unknown parameters are ignored, `+` is literal, `%3F` and `%23` decode as field data, and `n` is limited to 64 UTF-16 units (JS `.length`). Current builders emit `v, r, h, t, k, n[, c][, s]`, `v=2` with `c` exactly when given a secret and `v=1` otherwise, and percent-encode everything outside the RFC 3986 unreserved set with uppercase hex.
  Legacy inline links and their build vectors use the complete `request_ref`, `read`, `write` triple in that order after existing fields, in either version and envelope. HTTPS carries it only in the fragment; the legacy custom-scheme payload remains local. `request_ref` is exactly 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters; `read` and `write` are compact JSON string arrays, percent-encoded once with uppercase escapes (`[]` becomes `%5B%5D`). Each wire array must be sorted and distinct, either side may be empty, both cannot be empty, and a type may occur once on each side. Names must be catalog types (including workout and characteristics); writes must be writable. Producers sort and deduplicate before building. Ordinary phone `access_request` parsing continues to normalize arrays. Missing scope stays absent from preview JSON; present scope becomes `requested_scope: {request_ref, read, write}`. A later explicit `access_request` requires renewed explicit owner intent and phone availability.
  After the existing base/insecure checks, scope errors are ordered: missing `request_ref`, `read`, `write`; invalid reference; read then write JSON string-array structure and sorted/distinct order; both empty (`param=read`); read catalog, write catalog, write writability; envelope size (`param=scope`). All use `invalid_uri` with no raw values. The three legacy inline keys participate in the earlier encounter-order duplicate/percent/UTF-8 checks. Unknown keys still ignore malformed encoding.
  The transition parser keeps the legacy inline fit rule with no URI-length or item-count cap. Both a synthetic no-reason request and its largest reply must fit the historic 4096-byte serialized UTF-8 envelope, including marker, recipient HPKE, AEAD tag and base64url overhead. Pairing checks use `m_agent_999999` and `m_dev_999999`, envelope/reply timestamps `9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z`, and request creation `9999-12-30T23:59:59.999Z` with expiry exactly 24 hours later. The worst resolved reply gives every item `needs_health_settings`; the rate-limited refusal is also checked. Recheck actual member identifiers before applying access. No synthetic request is sent or admitted. Boundary vectors carry exact `envelope_bytes` for the request, resolved reply and refusal, including catalog-derived 4096-byte fitting and 4097-byte rejected replies. Pairing grants are explicit owner actions and bypass ordinary access-request admission quotas and decline cooldowns.
- **Pairing code and proof** (`pair-codes.json`): the code hashes the base64url text of `c` (not its bytes) and the proof is keyed by the 16 raw bytes of `c` over the base64url key strings; the choices are the last group and its two decoys as 3-digit strings sorted ascending, so the phone shows the same order everywhere; agents compare a received proof with the expected one in constant time on the decoded 32 bytes.
- **Trusted `ApplyCommand` fields**: `from` and `sync_identifier` come from the envelope sender and the hub, never from the agent. A `from` or `sync_identifier` key inside an agent's command is kept in the stored raw command but never reaches `to_apply`, so an agent cannot address HealthKit objects written for another hub or agent.
- **Command policy** (`command-policy.json`): first failure wins: unknown type, `write: false` or not allowlisted → `type_not_allowed`; a write (never a delete) whose type is outside the case's `scope.write` list, or any write when `scope.write` is `"none"` → `type_not_in_scope`; unknown op; the value not a finite JSON number; `unit` present but not a string or not in the catalog unit's family (an absent `unit` is the catalog unit, `"unit": null` is not); a missing or malformed `start`/`end`, `start > end`, an `end` later than the case's `now` + 1 h or `end − start` longer than the type's `max_span_s` (all `invalid`); then the value is converted with `((value * from.factor + from.offset) - to.offset) / to.factor` in IEEE doubles, in exactly this order (the same unit leaves it unchanged), and checked against `min` and `max` → `value_out_of_range`. A finite value whose conversion overflows to infinity is `value_out_of_range`, not `invalid`. Category writes keep the enum check; deletes skip the value checks. A case's optional `scope` is a full scope object (`read` and `write`, no other keys, each side `"all"`, `"none"` or a list of catalog names, `write` names writable), the grammar `setAgentScope` and `CoreTools.evaluateCommandInScope` accept; a case without it is evaluated with all/all. Optional `declined` is a sorted distinct list of declined write-type names (absent = empty). A `type_not_in_scope` rejection has `detail: "declined_by_user"` when its type is in that list. Invalid rejections carry the first failed check's `detail`: `unknown_op`, `bad_value`, `bad_unit`, `bad_category_value`, `bad_interval`, `end_in_future` or `span_too_long`; other reasons have no detail.
- **Canonical `to_apply`**: an allowed write reaches Swift and the ledger with the converted value and the catalog unit (unchanged when the agent already used it), so iOS writes in the catalog unit and the agent's unit is not kept on the phone.
- **Ack statuses** (`inner-messages.json` `sync_ack_deleted_by_user_kept`, `sync_drop_ack_rules`): `applied`, `rejected` and `deleted_by_user`; `reason` (`type_not_allowed`, `type_not_in_scope`, `value_out_of_range`, `healthkit_denied`, `invalid`; `sync_ack_type_not_in_scope`) is required for `rejected` and forbidden for the other two (dropped as an element); any other status drops only that ack. Optional `detail` follows `reason` and is emitted only on `rejected`, omitted when unknown, matching `^[a-z_]{1,32}$`. Its invalid-command codes are `end_in_future`, `span_too_long`, `bad_interval`, `bad_value`, `bad_unit`, `bad_category_value` and `unknown_op`; `type_not_in_scope` may carry `declined_by_user` for an explicitly declined write type. Unknown well-formed details are retained; a malformed/non-string detail or one on another status drops only `/acks/<index>/detail`, keeping the ack. Detail survives restart and same-version resend and has the same form in direct-server `results`. `sync_ack_detail_*` and `sync_ack_declined_by_user` pin these rules. An implementation that does not know `deleted_by_user` must still drop just that element, which is what makes the status backward compatible within v1.
- **Agent scope** (`inner-messages.json` `sync_scope_*`, `sync_without_scope_has_none`): `scope` is optional, after `more`, `{"read": …, "write": …}` with each side `"all"`, `"none"` (`sync_scope_none*`: the owner shares nothing, or lets the agent write nothing) or a non-empty list of names matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,63}$`; parsers deduplicate and sort the lists, keep names they do not know and ignore unknown keys inside the object. `["none"]` is a list with one name, never "nothing". Any other shape (not an object, `null`, a side missing, another word, `"NONE"`, a non-string or badly spelled name, an empty list) drops only the field: `/scope` is listed in `dropped` after the element drops and the message stays `ok`. The phone sends it in every relay sync message; a native webhook body has none. A parser that predates `"none"` drops such a scope as malformed; the phone still enforces each side independently: `read: "none"` stops Health-data uploads, while `write: "none"` rejects writes with `type_not_in_scope`.
- **Own deletions**: the phone reports `deleted_by_user` for a command only when the user deleted the object of the command's current version after it was `applied`: a deleted object whose sync identifier is exactly `syncky:<hub_id>:<paired agent member_id>:<command_id>` and whose `sync_version` equals the ledger's `last_version`. The phone reports it whatever the agent's read scope: a type the agent may write but not read is checked for such deletions too, and the own deletion is never uploaded as a `deleted` item. The deletions HealthKit makes for an update or a delete carry an older version and are never reported; every other `syncky:` object stays echo. Consumers may project `deleted_by_user` as terminal for that version; the thin agent retains every raw reply without a command ledger. The phone answers a resend of that version with `deleted_by_user` again.
- **`sync_version` is boundary-only**: the `collectedJson` deletions carry it from iOS to the core (`bridge-json.json` `collected_with_sync_version`), the inner parser ignores it as an unknown field, and it never reaches a relay message or a webhook body. The same holds for `user_entered` on samples (`collected_every_object_kind`), which only the Health Auto Export `symptoms` array uses.
- **Object kinds** (`inner-messages.json` `sync_state_of_mind`, `sync_scored_assessments`, `sync_audiogram`, `sync_activity_summary`, `sync_workout_*`, `sync_*_part` and their `sync_drop_*` cases): enumerated fields carry the names of the type's `enums` table in `types.json`, never raw values; an unknown name drops the sample. The workout's `location`, `metadata` and array fields are optional for parsers (defaults `location: "unknown"`, `metadata: {}`, empty arrays) and always written by emitters; a `statistics` entry whose `type` is not a catalog quantity is skipped, not dropped. An activity summary's uuid must be `activity_summary:<date>` and has no `start`, `end` or `source`; receivers replace a stored day when the envelope `seq` is higher (the characteristic rule) and never count it as a duplicate.
- **Interval sums** (`inner-messages.json` `sync_summaries`, `sync_summaries_only`, `sync_summaries_empty`, `sync_summaries_beside_raw_entries`, `sync_drop_summary_rules`, `sync_summaries_not_array`): a relay `sync` message may carry an optional top-level `summaries` array after `scope`. The phone uses it only for an agent whose `agent_info.version` is `0.1.4` or newer (three numeric parts compared as numbers; a suffix after `-` or `+` is ignored); an agent with an older, unreadable or unannounced version keeps receiving these types as raw samples. For such an agent the phone sends every quantity with `"interval_sums": true` in `types.json` (activity totals that a device accumulates: steps, energy, distances, flights, exercise, move and stand time, daylight and similar) there as Apple Health's sum per interval and no longer as raw samples. A cumulative quantity with `"interval_sums": false` is logged as separate entries whose time and source matter (`dietary_*` including water and caffeine, `insulin_delivery`, `inhaler_usage`, `number_of_alcoholic_beverages` and `number_of_times_fallen`); the phone sends it as raw samples to every agent and never in `summaries` (`sync_summaries_beside_raw_entries`). A summed element is `{type, unit, start, end, stat, value}` with `stat: "sum"`, the catalog unit, and an interval of exactly 900 seconds whose `start` is a multiple of 900 seconds since the Unix epoch (a UTC quarter hour). An element has no uuid and no source. Its key is `(device, type, start, end)`, where `device` is the envelope sender; receivers key by `start` and `end` and do not assume the length. A later element with the same key, in a later envelope `seq` or later in the same array, replaces the stored value; a receiver never adds the two. The phone resends an interval whenever its sum changes, including the interval in progress, sends `value: 0` for an interval it sent earlier that has become empty, and never sends an interval that had no data. The sums leave out objects written through Syncky. After a deletion the phone recomputes the last 7 days, so the interval of an older deleted sample may stay unchanged. `deleted` still lists deleted raw objects of these types. A receiver that also holds raw samples of the same device and type from an app version before 0.1.3 uses the summary for the time it covers. Parsers accept `sum` and `avg`, the catalog unit of a known quantity, `end` after `start` and a finite value, ignore unknown element keys, drop an invalid element as `/summaries/<i>` and a value that is not an array as `/summaries`; the message stays `ok`. `normalized` emits the array only when it has elements. Parsers that predate the array ignore it. Direct servers are unchanged: they receive raw samples, and daily summaries only in native history.
- **Series parts** (`series-parts.json`): a wire `workout_route` or `heartbeat_series` needs integer `part` and `parts` with `0 ≤ part < parts ≤ 100000` and `0 ≤ count ≤ 10^7`; anything else, including a missing `part`, drops with the single code `bad_part`. A bad tuple drops the whole part. Parts are keyed `(device, uuid, part)`: an identical repeat is ignored, a differing repeat or header makes the set inconsistent (discarded, later parts ignored for 7 days), a set completes when every index is present and the joined array length equals `count`, and an incomplete set expires after 7 days. The reassembled sample has no `part`/`parts` and equals `reassembled` exactly. Splitters cut by the emitted byte size, not by a point count, so `parts` only matches when an implementation emits the same bytes.
- **Webhook signatures**: the verifier compares the whole `v1=<lowercase hex>` header value in constant time, so uppercase hex is `bad_signature`.
- **CSV and line protocol bodies** (`webhook-requests.json` `csv_*`, `influx_*`): CSV uses CRLF, quotes a field only when it holds `,`, `"`, CR or LF, writes times in the sample's `local_offset_s` (`±HH:MM`) or `Z`, `user_entered` as `true`/`false` on sample rows and empty on characteristic and deletion rows, and a deletion as `type,uuid,,,,,deleted,,,`. Line protocol sorts tags by key, leaves out empty tags, escapes `\`, `,` and space (and `=` in tags), turns tabs and line breaks in tags and strings into spaces, and writes the start in nanoseconds. Numbers use the JSON number spelling of the core (`812`, not `812.0`).
- **Basic auth** (`native_basic_signed`, `csv_basic_signed_every_kind`): `Authorization: Basic base64(<auth.user>:<token secret>)` after the signature headers; the user is printable ASCII without `:`.
- **Server replies and results** (`test-vectors/webhook-exchanges.json`): a reply is signed `X-Syncky-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>` over `<X-Syncky-Delivery of the request>.<t>.<raw reply body>`, unlike the request signature, which has its own timestamp header; the results request body is `{"v":1,"type":"results","results":[…]}` whose entries have the ack shape of `inner-sync.schema.json` (`command_id`, `version`, `status`, `reason`), sent with `X-Syncky-Kind: results` instead of `X-Syncky-Format`. The file's cases carry a `kind`. A `reply` case is one server reply as the phone checks it: `url` (http or https), `signing`, `secret`, the request's `delivery`, `t`, the phone's clock `now`, `content_type`, `body`, `signature` (or null), `signature_valid` (the signature is the exact one for `delivery`, `t` and `body`, whatever the time window) and `expect`, which is `{"verdict":"commands","count":n}`, `{"verdict":"empty"}` or `{"verdict":"ignored","reason":…}` with the reasons `too_large`, `not_json`, `not_commands`, `unsigned` and `bad_signature`. The http replies answer request 0 of `webhook-requests.json` `native_bearer_signed_every_kind` (its `X-Syncky-Delivery`, its HMAC secret and its timestamp as `t`), so a receiver replaying that request signs `signed_http` byte for byte; `signed_http` is two writes, `c_1` `dietary_water` and `c_2` `apple_exercise_time`, and `signed_http_delete` deletes `c_1` (version 2) in a later exchange. The `results_request` case is what the phone sends after `signed_http` (`c_1` applied, `c_2` rejected `type_not_allowed`), and one `test_request` per format is the Check-connection request (the format's body for no changes, `delivery.test: true` in native, an empty influx body); both carry the `destination`, its `secrets`, and the byte-exact `headers` and `body`. Phone/schema tests cover these reply and request bytes; the agent's `selftest` checks `webhook-signatures.json`. `examples/minimal-server` signs `signed_http` byte for byte.
- **Sync identifiers per source**: agent `syncky:<hub_id>:<member_id>:<command_id>`, server `syncky:wh_<id>:<command_id>`, file import `syncky:import:<16 hex>:<row>`; the source is always local (the pairing, the destination, the file's hash), never taken from a reply or a file.
- **Numbers**: integers in JSON bodies are value-based (`1`, `1.0`, `1e0` are 1; fractional, string, boolean, null, negative and ≥ 2^53 values are not integers). Emitters write an integral finite value as a JSON integer (`812`, not `812.0`). Fractional formatting is not pinned; compare by value.
- **Timestamps**: emit UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` when the milliseconds are 0, otherwise exactly 3 fraction digits (sub-millisecond truncated). Accept `Z`/`z` or `±HH:MM`, uppercase or lowercase `t`, and 0–9 fraction digits; reject everything else, including calendar-invalid dates, hour 24 and `:60`.

## Schema rules

- JSON Schema 2020-12. Each file has an `$id` (`https://syncky.app/protocol/schemas/<file>`) and a `$defs` map; validate a document against `<$id>#/$defs/<name>`.
- Only local `#/$defs/…` refs, no cross-file refs (the vector schema carries its own copy of the submitted envelope).
- `pattern`, never the `format` keyword, so Ajv `strict: true` and networknt need no format plugins. Calendar validity of timestamps (Feb 30) and base64url canonical tails are checked by the implementations, not by the schemas.
- The schemas stay Ajv-strict clean: an explicit `type` next to every type-specific keyword, `anyOf` instead of type arrays, and every `required` name declared in the same schema's `properties`. The core checks these rules together with the meta-schema.
- Envelopes reject unknown top-level keys; inner messages, system events and samples allow them. Inner-message timestamps use the emit form (see Timestamps above); envelope and system-event timestamps use the accept form.
- In `inner-messages.json` and `bridge-json.json`, the `json` field of a case is the exact JSON text as a string, so unparsable and non-object inputs are representable and the bytes are preserved.

## Diagnostics data and consent controls

New senders add optional visible envelope metadata `diagnostics=request|reply|archive`: request/reply require `kind=control`, archive requires `kind=data`; ordinary traffic omits it and system events cannot carry it. This reveals the claimed diagnostics purpose to Relay, which checks shape and routes traffic but cannot decrypt or verify the inner contents. Both HPKE Auth and payload AEAD bind the marker after any `|control` suffix as `|diagnostics=<value>`; updated receivers reject marker/inner mismatch before dispatch and never fall back to legacy AAD. Unmarked older diagnostics and already-sealed legacy retries remain accepted unchanged. Older receivers cannot open honestly marked traffic and must update; deploy relay support before using new senders and update both endpoints together, without stripping markers on errors.

A newly queued marked request triggers a best-effort generic visible `diagnostics_request` push on every plan, outside ordinary push scheduling. It carries the already-visible envelope `msg_id`, no request reference or report contents. Remote taps match that id to the authenticated pending request; local `diagnostics-request-<ref>` taps match the exact reference. A notification tap opens Review for its matching pending request once available; expired, answered, replaced, unmatched or re-paired notices only open Diagnostics without selecting another request. Receipt alone prepares nothing, and only Confirm sends the approved preview.

Envelope `v=1` and kinds remain `data`, `control` and relay-generated `system`; the optional `diagnostics` field adds visible purpose metadata without a new kind or version. `type=diagnostics` is a phone-to-agent data inner, never a Health sample or command. The complete canonical UTF-8 JSON is at most 180000 bytes, sent to one confirmed agent within the 262144-byte serialized envelope cap. Its `archive_ref`, optional `request_ref` and peer references are 32 lowercase hex characters, derived with domain-separated SHA-256; the diagnostics report contains closed findings, aggregate counts, times, build metadata and safe history, never raw hub/member ids, names, credentials, URLs, Health values/type names or command payloads. Unknown fields are rejected. `inner-messages.json` pins normalization, invalid fields, bounds and cross-kind rejection; `envelopes.json` pins encrypted diagnostics and request/reply round trips. Vector bytes win over prose.

Canonical submitted JSON orders the existing required fields `v, msg_id, kind, from, created_at, recipients, nonce, ciphertext`, inserting `access` or `diagnostics` immediately after `kind` when present. Null, empty, unknown and incompatible marker values are invalid. Missing marker preserves the prior canonical bytes. Exact AAD in both crypto layers is UTF-8 of `syncky-v1|<hub_id>|<msg_id>|<from>` + (`|control` for control) + (`|diagnostics=<value>` when present), in that fixed order; HPKE info stays `syncky-cek-v1`. Request/control must decrypt to `diagnostics_request`, reply/control to `diagnostics_reply`, archive/data to `diagnostics`. A mismatch is `inner_invalid`; stripped, added or changed markers fail authentication, with no legacy-AAD fallback. The generated positive, shape and negative vectors cover these rules while retaining unmarked cases. A paired sender can claim a lane with legacy-AAD ciphertext that an old receiver may still act on; the small relay lane bounds this residual abuse. Marker authentication protects updated recipients and does not let Relay verify contents.

`diagnostics_request` is an agent-to-phone encrypted control inner with `request_ref`, `created_at` and `expires_at` exactly 24 hours later. `diagnostics_reply` goes back with that reference and `outcome=declined|expired`; reasons are `user`, `pending_limit`, `rate_limited` for declined or `deadline` for expired. Controls retain the 4096-byte envelope cap. A confirmed diagnostics report carries the request reference. Consumers correlate it through the durable raw inbox; there is no agent-local request state or diagnostics validator. Relay acceptance and transport ACK alone do not prove diagnostics report receipt. Old clients may skip unknown controls and the request expires; the minimal agent authenticates/decrypts data, generically skips non-sync contents and persists/ACKs without diagnostics report storage.

Request arrival only records pending state. A matching notification tap opens Review; Home opens Diagnostics. Review prepares and freezes the preview, View/Download expose those bytes, Confirm authorizes those same bytes to that agent, and Decline queues only a reply. Rebuilding invalidates consent. The phone keeps one pending request per agent and a 24-hour expiry; phone retries do not reset deadlines. The phone permits at most one diagnostics report per rolling 24 hours per agent pairing, counting both manual Send and a confirmed request on its own clock; Send and Confirm show when they become available again. View and Download are unlimited. The thin agent sends explicitly requested JSON through generic CLI/MCP send and reads diagnostics or diagnostics_reply through inbox. It imposes no local cooldown or request admission policy; the phone owns those decisions. Sealed outbox retries and raw inbox persistence use protected files, without SQLite. Marked traffic uses an independent relay lane on every plan: 30 new envelopes per hub per UTC day and at most 2 MiB/100 outstanding rows per hub by default, outside ordinary control quotas, agent data-send budgets and general queue capacity. Its token RPM allowance is separate from ordinary calls, including ACKs. HTTP `429 rate_limited` distinguishes `details.reason=diagnostics_quota` (Retry-After to UTC midnight), `diagnostics_queue_full` (300 seconds) and ordinary `queue_full`; RPM refusals have no lane-specific reason. Identical accepted retries spend no new daily/queue quota. Legacy unmarked traffic retains ordinary relay accounting. The diagnostics outbox lane retries independently of ordinary sends.

Local Check sends nothing. Separate explicit evidence refresh and diagnostics report preparation may read device-member-authenticated `GET /v1/hub/diagnostics` without diagnostics upload or sync. It returns caller-only push attempts beside last phone contact, existing agent poll/ACK evidence and scoped queue counts. APNs 200 means accepted, not delivered or proof of why iOS did not run. History is bounded to the hub's newest 50 sends within 48 hours; missing/stale evidence remains unknown. A missing route is explicit `unsupported_route`, while local Check/View/Download remain usable. Marked diagnostics reports retain `402 hub_unpaid|hub_suspended`; marked requests/replies remain admissible in active, unpaid and suspended hubs under diagnostics limits.

Phone history and manual pending diagnostics report retries expire after 48 hours; request-bound diagnostics reports stop sending at the original 24-hour request deadline. Matching pre-expiry diagnostics report/decline sends can resolve a local deadline expiry when processed within 48 hours of sending; pairing changes and post-expiry sends remain rejected. Terminal reply retries last 48 hours from the decision, independently of that request deadline. The thin agent retains every authentic diagnostics record in its raw inbox for 30 days from receipt, including repeated archive references under new envelopes. Read operations do not prune; receive startup/daily pruning and explicit owner-approved forget after revocation follow the ordinary inbox rules. Phone pruning runs when the app next executes. User-controlled downloaded copies and support attachments follow their destination's retention. Diagnostics are neither identity proof nor a complete access export; use the app's Privacy requests flow for verified Relay requests.

## Health access controls

`access: "request" | "reply"` is optional visible metadata on `kind=control` only, mapping to authenticated `access_request` (agent → confirmed phone) or `access_reply` (phone → requesting agent). `access` and `diagnostics` are mutually exclusive; neither appears on relay `system` events. Reject null, unknown, malformed, dual or wrong-kind markers. New access inners require the marker; the decrypted type must match it before dispatch, pairing exceptions or state mutation. The relay validates shape and retains the marker, but cannot verify encrypted semantics.

Canonical envelope order is `v, msg_id, kind, access?, diagnostics?, from, created_at, recipients, nonce, ciphertext`. Both HPKE Auth and payload AEAD use UTF-8 `syncky-v1|<hub_id>|<msg_id>|<from>` followed by optional `|control`, optional `|diagnostics=<value>`, optional `|access=<value>` in that order. Mutual exclusion permits at most one marker suffix. Unmarked/diagnostics bytes are unchanged. Added, stripped or changed markers and legacy-AAD ciphertext with an attached marker fail authentication; never fall back, strip a marker or reseal a persisted retry. Submission keys are strict; delivery still tolerates unrelated extra keys, but a malformed present marker is never absent.

Both inners are v1. `access_request` fields are `v, type, request_ref, created_at, expires_at, read, write` and optional `reason`. The reference is 32 lowercase hex characters; timestamps must satisfy an original positive interval of at most 24 hours (`0 < expires_at - created_at <= 24h`) and retain a positive interval of at most 24 hours after normalization to persisted millisecond precision. A collapsing interval is invalid with `detail: ttl`; general RFC 3339 nanosecond parsing remains accepted. Required read/write arrays are jointly nonempty; the phone sorts and deduplicates each array, and the same name may occur on both sides. Validate read catalog/scope names (including `workout` and characteristics) and writability for writes independently of current scope. Reason is literal plain text, at most 200 Unicode code points, with invalid Unicode rejected; never interpret it as instructions or markup.

Access-request producers use finite positive TTL up to 24 hours (`0 < expires_at - created_at <= 24h`); the agent's `--validate` and MCP enforce that bound and reject malformed timestamps. Keep 24-hour examples as defaults; the phone sorts and deduplicates each array.

`access_reply` fields are `v, type, request_ref, decided_at, outcome, read, write`, with request-level `next_available_at` only for limit outcomes and optional `detail` only for `invalid`. Arrays are sorted by type and unique per side. Owner items have only `{type, outcome}` with `allowed`, `declined` or `needs_health_settings`. A filtered position has `{type, outcome: "refused", reason, next_available_at}`; reason is `requested_recently` or `declined_recently`, and its availability is required. Owner outcomes forbid refusal fields. Stored refusal times may precede a later root decision: preserve the filtering snapshot even if its wait ends while consent is open.

| Request case | Reply |
| --- | --- |
| Some eligible positions | One terminal `resolved` combines owner outcomes for shown positions with refused items for filtered positions; no request-level availability. |
| All positions time-filtered | Immediate `filtered`, nonempty refused-only sides, without a consent sheet or admission event. |
| Five-event ceiling | `rate_limited`, empty sides, `limit_reason: daily_ceiling` and request-level `next_available_at`. |
| Pending root already amended three times | `rate_limited`, empty sides, `limit_reason: amendment_limit` and guaranteed availability at the original root expiry, possibly later if the daily ceiling also applies. |
| Eligible amendment | Immediate `merged` under its own ref, required `merged_into` naming the root, refused-only sides for filtered positions (possibly empty). This acknowledges correlation and grants nothing. |
| Owner decides merged root | One terminal `resolved` under the root ref with the canonical union and `merged_refs` listing up to three admitted aliases. |
| Root expires | `expired`, empty sides and `merged_refs` for admitted aliases. No invented per-item decisions. |
| Invalid input or amendment | `invalid`, empty sides and optional value-free detail under its own usable ref. The pending root is unchanged. |

`pending_limit` and `invalid` have empty read/write arrays; the compatibility `pending_limit` requires request-level availability. Invalid detail is one of `unknown_type`, `not_writable`, `ttl`, `empty`, `reason_too_long`, `malformed`, `created_in_future`, `too_large`. Unknown-catalog or non-writable positions invalidate the whole request before filtering. An unusable reference prevents a correlatable reply; bounded refusal/reply queues can also prevent a reply under backlog. Never infer consent from silence.

`filtered` and `merged` forbid request-level availability, detail and limit reason. Only `merged` permits and requires `merged_into`. Only terminal `resolved`/`expired` may carry nonempty `merged_refs`; omit it for unamended roots and pairing grants. Refs are distinct 32-lowercase-hex values; aliases are sorted, unique, bounded to three and exclude the root. New `rate_limited` replies include `limit_reason`; receivers accept its absence in legacy replies. Other field combinations are rejected. Strict field/direction/timestamp rules live in [inner-system.schema.json](schemas/inner-system.schema.json), with marker shape in [envelope.schema.json](schemas/envelope.schema.json); Kotlin additionally enforces ordering and correlation invariants.

Correlate each alias acknowledgement with its root terminal reply, retaining both authenticated records regardless of arrival order. The canonical union contains each submitted side/type once across the root and admitted amendments, so it can exceed the original request's arrays. A shown position's owner outcome wins over a repeated refusal in an alias acknowledgement; a later eligible addition supersedes an earlier refusal for that position. Otherwise retain its latest refusal snapshot. Filtered, invalid and capped requests are not merged aliases. Never reopen a committed decision on replay. Pairing replies retain exact requested-item/ref matching and no aliases.

There is no item-count cap: before admission or amendment, both the serialized UTF-8 request envelope and the largest legal reply/acknowledgement must fit the 131072-byte access envelope cap, including refusal fields, three aliases, timestamps, AEAD tag, base64url expansion and HPKE recipient overhead. A merged union must fit even when each individual request fits. Reject an oversized amendment as `invalid/too_large` without changing the root; never split automatically.

From phone 0.1.3, the phone keeps one pending request per agent binding and five admitted events per rolling 24 hours, counting roots and at most three admitted amendments per pending request. Duplicate transport/ref retries, invalid and fully filtered requests consume no admission. Use phone time when a position is admitted, tracking read and write independently: each has a 24-hour requested-at wait. Only owner-declined shown types start a seven-day type-wide wait covering both sides. When both waits apply, use `declined_recently` and the later availability; equality at the boundary is eligible. Filtering resets neither timestamp and creates no decline. Choices made at pairing have no quota; a type declined at pairing starts the same seven-day wait. Pairing grants create no requested-at record, admission event or amendment count. Pairing declines do create the seven-day decline wait across read and write.

Validate shape/catalog/writability/size first, then expiry, then filter. With at least one eligible addition, check the five-event ceiling before the amendment cap. Daily availability is the oldest of the five active admissions plus 24 hours; when both caps apply use the later guaranteed availability with `daily_ceiling` precedence. The owner may answer before the root expires; a subsequent request then starts a new root, subject to type waits and the ceiling. Previously approved types do not block other eligible types. Send only the remaining needed types with explicit approval. Never automatically evade a wait by changing refs/reasons or splitting/resending filtered requests.

An admitted amendment joins the existing pending read/write union, preserving its original reason, creation time and expiry; it never extends that deadline. Repeated shown positions remain in the union but are refused as recent for the incoming alias. Added positions require fresh owner choices; a changed union invalidates stale consent intents. Already-expired requests receive `expired`; five-minute future skew and an admission-plus-24-hour clamp follow diagnostics. The phone persists decisions, requested-at records, admissions, refusals, aliases and byte-identical sealed retries under the pairing identity. Alias acknowledgement retries stop at the earlier of the incoming and root deadlines; root terminal retries stop at the unchanged root deadline. Revoke/unpair/re-pair clears stale work. The thin agent retains every raw reply with no local admission/cooldown policy, correlating ordinary merged response waits to the root. It never updates effective scope from an access reply.

Queued and transport ACK mean persistence, not user consent. Only explicit phone confirmation changes selection and stored scope; a reply alone never changes cached effective scope, which arrives on the next ordinary sync. For post-pairing access requests, Allow adds only approved types to Health selection, without selecting their categories. Existing selected categories and individually allowed types are preserved. Allowed writes add only the approved write types to the app allowance and request Health sharing only for those exact types, without adding reads; agent scope and iOS write permission still apply. Existing read `all` stays `all` and follows later Health selection changes. Approved reads turn `none` into a chosen list and are unioned and sorted into existing read lists. If writing was off or the agent's effective write allowance was empty, its write scope becomes only the approved write types, even from `all` or an absent scope; otherwise existing write scope is unioned as before. Decline revokes nothing. Both `allowed` and `needs_health_settings` mean Allow in Syncky. Health read authorization is unobservable; successful sheet completion and empty data prove neither a grant nor denial. Previously answered reads and denied/undetermined writes need conditional Health settings guidance. Asking never authorizes writing a Health value.

Access uses the general relay lane with shared token RPM, non-active control quota and ordinary queue caps/429 Retry-After. At defaults this is 60 bearer attempts per member per fixed minute, 10000 general stored rows per sender and 67108864 general stored bytes per hub (512 access bodies at the cap in an otherwise empty hub). On unpaid or suspended hubs the shared 50 accepted controls per member per UTC day permit up to 6553600 access bytes per member per day before other bounds. Identical E10 duplicates spend neither queue space nor accepted-control quota. A paired sender can attach a valid access marker to arbitrary ciphertext within the transport caps. Recipients authenticate it and reject mismatched inner content. It has no diagnostics exemption or relay lifecycle state. Endpoint scheduling stays independent of diagnostics and ordinary sends. An alert admitted for a newly accepted request queues a generic visible `access_request` alert on every plan, with category `access_request`, latest `msg_id` and collapse id `access_request:<opaque value>`. A random per-agent value scoped to its hub persists across token rotation and process restart; no name, raw member id, type, reason or request reference reaches APNs. Queued replacement coalesces requests/amendments for that agent without adding Health types or values; live notification replacement remains device-dependent. Relay allows one visible access alert per sender per hub every five minutes and at most five visible alerts per rolling 24 hours. One admission covers all eligible device tokens; no token means no admission, identical envelope retries spend nothing, and APNs failure gives no refund. This opaque-envelope budget is separate from phone semantic admission. A suppressed alert leaves the encrypted request queued, preserves any already queued collapsed alert, and schedules an ordinary silent wake only under the existing active-plan, recipient and silent-budget rules. Unfetched, unexpired access requests remain eligible for pending-wake retries and contact checks. There is no delayed visible alert. Delivery is best effort: on the next open, the app fetches queued requests and presents those admitted by the phone even if no wake arrived. Suppression alone neither rejects the request nor consumes phone semantic admission; neither a push nor relay acceptance proves consent. Receipt/tap never grants access or presents Health authorization. Exact remote root/admitted-amendment msg-id or local reference routing selects only the live matching root under the current pairing; stale notices never select another request.

Deploy relay support before updated senders, and update both endpoints. This is a deliberate v1 reply extension: old strict schema consumers reject the new shapes and old callers cannot correlate merged roots; update their schemas and guidance together. Older thin agents can retain raw authenticated replies, while old clients may fail to open or skip access controls; safely ACK poison messages, allow expiry and update, never downgrade AAD. Minimal/browser examples authenticate the marker/inner match and skip unsupported access controls without exposing their contents; their cursor/ACK and later sync processing continue. Request/decision storage and consent UI belong to the phone; the thin agent offers generic send/inbox and retains raw messages.

The thin agent reads the generated messages.json table and bundled/verified inner schemas for optional send validation. It retains authenticated raw JSON for 30 days without a Health parser, ledger or SQLite; phone/schema tests own feature-policy and reassembly conformance.

## Scope release

The phone applies the effective agent read scope to workout `statistics` and `activities[].statistics`, retaining every statistic value only for allowed quantity types. It removes `energy_kcal` unless `active_energy_burned` is allowed. For `distance_m`, it uses this item's pre-filter top-level `statistics`: at least one recognized distance source must have a valid numeric `sum`, and every contributing source must be allowed. Missing or malformed distance provenance removes the alias; an unrelated excluded catalog distance type has no effect. Permitted typed statistics, workout structure and order remain; removed metrics do not increase the enclosing-item drop count. The separate `activity_summary` fields and direct-server behavior remain unchanged. Filtering runs before collection and again before encryption, including after a `scope_release` fetched in that run. Generated `scope-filter.json` cases pin these rules, including all/none scopes and released or mixed distance sources.

`scope_release` (agent → confirmed phone) is an unmarked `kind=control` message with which an agent gives up Health types it no longer needs: `{"v":1,"type":"scope_release","read":[…],"write":[…]}`. Both arrays are required and jointly nonempty; names are catalog scope names (types, `workout`, characteristics), write names must be writable. The phone sorts and deduplicates each side; the canonical emitted form is sorted and unique. An unknown name, a non-writable write name, an extra key or two empty sides make the message `invalid` and the phone drops it (`inner-messages.json` `system_scope_release*`).

The message only reduces access, so the phone applies it at once without owner confirmation: it removes the named types from this agent's stored scope and from its pairing grant, rejects pending and later writes for released write types with `type_not_in_scope`, and stops observing types that only this agent's pairing grant needed. A stored `all` side stays `all` with the released names excluded, so types the owner allows later still reach the agent. The owner's Health selection, the app write allowance and iOS permissions are untouched, and a name outside the agent's scope is a no-op. A released type returns through an ordinary `access_request` or the owner's Connections screen.

There is no reply and no marker. The phone always announces its effective scope in the next sync message after a valid release, changed or not; the agent compares that scope with what it released. A phone app older than 0.1.4 skips the type as `unknown_system_type` and keeps announcing the old scope, which the thin agent reports as `not_supported`. Replays are skipped by envelope `msg_id` like every phone-bound control message, and a release first fetched more than 7 days after its `msg_id` time is ignored as stale, which the agent also sees as an unchanged scope. The relay treats it as ordinary control traffic with no state of its own.
